opening.argument: The video explains how YouTube monetization works through specific eligibility and payment conditions: viewers must reach 1,000 subscribers and 4,000 hours of watch time, undergo YouTube review, provide payment information, and accumulate a $100 advertising-revenue threshold. It also presents an approximate view-based payment rate, framing the dollar amounts as platform revenue conditions rather than a solicitation for payment or investment. The separately linked course is identified as a learning product. Although some estimates and claims may be uncertain, the available evidence shows no viewer losses or completed payment outcomes. The video therefore functions as an educational explanation of YouTube monetization and related operational steps.

citations.quote: You're gonna have to get 1,000 people to subscribe to your new channel, and on top of that you're gonna have to get 4,000 hours worth of time of your videos watched in a 12 month period.

Your channel was then going to get reviewed from YouTube and if everything goes well, within the next 30 days, you'll receive an email from YouTube telling you that your channel has been activated and can now receive payments.
Once you've been approved your channel is going to have to collect its $100 in total from the adverts shown on your videos before you get your first payment.
In general, YouTube pays you around $2 for every thousand views you get
